case: Deterministic finite-f64 CSV and JSON consumer parity
change: Expand the seeded raw-bit sample from 256 values to 65,536 finite IEEE-754 bit patterns, including subnormals; reject exponent-all-ones patterns so the corpus contains only finite values.
contract: Every corpus value round-trips through default CSV export, typed DOUBLE PRECISION import and JSON export/parse with exact to_bits() equality.
All 86,012 expected entries are finite; the raw-bit sample is deterministic from a fixed xorshift seed.
The independent expected values are constructed from explicit IEEE-754 bit patterns and checked against imported/parsed bits.

focused_test.command: rtk proxy cargo test --manifest-path linux/Cargo.toml -p tablepro-core --lib value_contract_csv_and_json_round_trip_seeded_finite_float_bits

core_library_suite.command: rtk proxy cargo test --manifest-path linux/Cargo.toml -p tablepro-core --lib

clippy.command: rtk proxy cargo clippy --manifest-path linux/Cargo.toml -p tablepro-core --all-targets -- -D warnings

validation.format: rtk proxy cargo fmt --manifest-path linux/Cargo.toml --all -- --check passed

remaining: The corpus is deterministic broad coverage, not exhaustive enumeration of every finite f64 encoding.
Spreadsheet-application import and other consumer/session combinations remain open.
